DCE iron ore futures today.. the main contract closed 780.5. an increase of 0.06% throughout the day; some traders were negative to sell;Some steel mills tended to be wait-and-see, and purchased on demand. today's overall market transacƟon atmosphere in general. PBF at Shandong port dealt 775- 780 yuan/mt; the same as last Friday. PBF at Tangshan port dealt 794-800 yuan/mt; the same as last Friday. SMM's global iron ore shipment volume was 30.27 million tons, a decrease of 0.9% compared to the previous period. Among them, Australia shipped 15.16 million tons, a slight decrease of 6.5% compared to the previous period; Brazil shipped 8.54 million tons, an increase of 17.9% compared to the previous period; SMM China's total amount of iron ore arriving at the port was 25.67 million tons, a month on month decrease of 6.49%. The change in shipping volume for this period is relatively small. The arrival volume has decreased due to the impact of previous shipments and recent typhoon weather. As the weather improves and the impact decreases, there is still room for an increase in estimated arrival volume. The supply of iron ore remains loose. But considering the increasing losses of steel mills, the number of short-term blast furnace maintenance will increase. The demand for iron ore has decreased, and the price of ore is under pressure and fluctuating.

DCE iron ore futures market falling sharply trends, the main contract closed 756, an decrease of 2.77% throughout the day;Traders are feeling indifferent about shipping; steel mills are cautious and mainly purchasing on demand. The overall market atmosphere today is average. In Shandong, the transaction price of PB powder is between 755-760 yuan/ton, a decrease of 15-20 yuan/ton compared to yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction price of PB powder is between 770-775 yuan/ton, a decrease of 20-25 yuan/ton compared to yesterday. According to SMM statistics, the impact of blast furnace maintenance on iron water this week (July 27th to August 2nd) was 109.91 million tons, an increase of 7.24 million tons compared to last week. The current trend of iron water is declining, weakening the support for iron powder demand, and exacerbating the losses of steel mills. Some steel mills have gradually increased their blast furnace maintenance plans. It is expected that short-term iron ore prices will predominantly fluctuate weakly.

DCE iron ore futures continued to fluctuate in a day，the main contract closed 749，an increase of 0.07% throughout the day.Traders are shipping with general sentiment; steel mills are cautious and still focus on need-based procurement. The overall market transaction atmos- phere is moderate today. In Shandong, the transaction price of PB powder is 765-770 yuan/ton, an increase of 5-10 yuan/ton compared to yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction price of PB powder is 780-785 yuan/ton, an increase of 5-10 yuan/ton compared to yesterday. According to SMM research, on July 31, the blast furnace operating rate was 92.91%, a decrease of 0.7% compared to the previous month. The blast furnace capacity utilization rate was 94.94%, a decrease of 0.58% compared to the previous month. The average daily pig iron production of sample steel mills is 2.283 million tons, a decrease of 0.71 million tons compared to the previous month. The current pig iron production shows a downward trend, weakening support for iron ore prices. It is expected that iron ore prices will show weak and stable fluctuations in the short term.

text:
DCE iron ore futures rose largely today, the main contract closed 767, an increase of 2.47% throughout the day. Tradersexhibited moderate selling sentiment, while steel mills remained cautious and primarily adopted a on-demand procurement strategy. Today's overall market transaction atmosphere was average. In the Shandong region, PB fines traded at 775-785 RMB/ton, showing an increase of 10-15 RMB/ton compared to yesterday; in the Tangshan region, PB fines traded at 795-800 RMB/ton, also up by 10-15 RMB/ton from the previous day. According to SMM statistics, due to some restocking needs from steel mills, total inventory at the ten major ports showed a slight decline this week. On the demand side, today's apparent demand data for the five major steel products indicated that demand for rebar and wire rod remained weak, exerting some pressure on the upward movement of ore prices. It is expected that in the short term, iron ore prices will exhibit a narrow range of fluctuation.

DCE iron ore futures today. the main contract I2501 closed 776.5. an increase of 1.97% throughout the day; The traders'enthusiasm for shipping is moderate; Steel mills are cautiously observing, with general willingness to purchase. The overall market trading atmosphere was sluggish today. PBF at Shandong port dealt 790 yuan/mt; the same as last Friday. PBF at Tangshan port dealt 805 yuan/mt; the same as last Friday. According to SMM data, global iron ore shipments reached 32.77 million mt, up 8.3% MoM. Among them, shipments from Australia and non-mainstream mines increased, while shipments from Brazil decreased. The SMM report shows that China's iron ore port arrivals totaled 19.6 million mt, a sharp drop of 28.6% MoM. Demand side, due to severe losses faced by steel mills and increased blast furnace maintenance, pig iron output is expected to decline significantly this week. However, as the market releases pessimistic sentiment, overall sentiment has improved. Additionally, the expected increase in monetary policy may have some impact on the market, but in the short term, the upward momentum for ore prices is insufficient, and they are expected to remain narrowly fluctuating.

DCE iron ore futures weakly, today. the main contract I2501 closed 763. an decrease of 1.42% throughout the day;Traders sold according to market conditions, while steel mills restocked as needed. The overall market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 780-785 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 795 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to SMM statistics, the impact of blast furnace maintenance on pig iron production this week was 1.0662 million mt, an increase of 33,000 mt MoM. Next week, the impact of blast furnace maintenance on pig iron production is expected to be 1.2153 million mt, a decrease of 149,100 mt MoM. In August, the reduction in pig iron production was significant, leading to a noticeable decline in iron ore demand. The supply-demand mismatch for iron ore increased, limiting the rise in iron ore prices. Considering that end-user demand remains in the offseason, market sentiment is not opƟmisƟc, and iron ore prices are expected to fluctuate weakly in the short term.

DCE iron ore futures weakly throughout the day, the main contract I2501 closed 749, down 2.41% for the day. Tradersshowed a general willingness to sell, while steel mills procured at lower prices. The overall market transaction atmosphere was sluggish today. In Shandong, the transaction price of PB fines was 770-775 yuan/mt, down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction price of PB fines was 785 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to an SMM survey, on August 7, the operating rate of blast furnaces surveyed by SMM was 92.37%, down 0.54% MoM. The capacity utilization rate of blast furnaces was 94.50%, down 0.44% MoM. The average daily pig iron output of the sample steel mills was 2.2672 million mt, down 15,800 mt MoM. However, according to the General Administration of Customs, China's iron ore imports in July increased by 5.4% MoM to 10,281,300 mt. The supply-demand mismatch of iron ore increased, suppressing iron ore prices. In the short term, iron ore prices may continue to fluctuate weakly.

DCE iron ore futures saw a significant decline, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 729.5 yuan/mt, down 3.63% for the day.Traders' willingness to sell decreased, and steel mills mainly restocked as needed. The overall market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 750-765 yuan/mt, down 5-15 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 765-780 yuan/mt, down 5-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. Today, the apparent demand for rebar and HRC declined significantly, and the accumulation rate of hot-rolled coil inventory accelerated. Overall steel demand continued to shrink, and the number of blast furnace maintenance is expected to increase further, intensifying negative feedback pressure. Iron ore prices plummeted, hitting a new low in nearly four months. Consider- ing the potential further decline in future iron ore demand, iron ore prices may remain weak and volatile in the short term.

DCE iron ore futures saw a significant rebound in the morning, but fell back again in the afternoon, ending the day with a strong oscillation.The most-traded contract I2501 finally closed at 741.5 yuan/mt, up 0.27% for the day. Traders followed the market trend to sell; steel mills had fewer inquiries as the weekend approached. Overall market transactions were average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 760-770 yuan/mt, up 5-15 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 775-780 yuan/mt, up 5-15 yuan/mt from yesterday As of August 9, the total inventory at the 35 ports tracked by SMM was 146.68 million mt, down 610,000 mt MoM, up 30.32 million mt YoY. Port inventories have decreased for two consecutive weeks, mainly due to a recent decline in port unloading efficiency, leading to a significant reduction in arrivals. Currently, port inventories remain at a high level, putting pressure on ore prices. Additionally, considering that pig iron production may significantly decrease next week, the short-term fundamentals of iron ore remain weak, making it difficult for ore prices to find upward momentum.

DCE iron ore futures hit a new low, with the market showing weak and volatile performance throughout the day. The most-traded contractI2501 finally closed at 734 yuan/mt, down 1.08% for the day. Traders showed moderate enthusiasm for selling; steel mills were cautiously observing, with some planning tenders. Overall market transaction sentiment was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 750-760 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt WoW; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 770-775 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt WoW. SMM reported global iron ore shipments at 31.87 million mt, down 2.8% WoW. Shipments from Australia were 16.75 million mt, down 7.3% WoW; shipments from Australia to China accounted for 82.1% of Australia's total shipments, down 4.8% WoW. Shipments from Brazil were 8.24 million mt, up 14% WoW; shipments from Brazil to China accounted for 56.4% of Brazil's total shipments, up 98.7% WoW. SMM reported China's iron ore arrivals at 26.11 million mt, up 33.22% WoW. Iron ore supply remains relatively ample. However, blast furnace maintenance continued to increase this week, and the market estimates a further significant decline in pig iron output, puƫng pressure on iron ore prices. In the short term, iron ore prices lack upward momentum and are expected to continue a weak and volatile trend.

text:
DCE iron ore futures moved downwards after a higher opening, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 734 yuan/mt, unchangedfrom yesterday. Traders showed weak enthusiasm for selling; steel mills were cautiously observing, with average purchasing willingness. The overall market transaction atmosphere was sluggish today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 755- 760 yuan/mt, basically flat compared to yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 770-775 yuan/mt, also flat compared to yesterday. In the morning, iron ore prices rebounded slightly, but the end-user market remained sluggish, lacking upward momentum. According to SMM's statistics on blast furnace maintenance, this week's blast furnace maintenance led to a reduction in pig iron output by over 80,000 mt. Under the pressure of negative feedback, the momentum for iron ore price rebound is insufficient, and it may continue to bottom out and operate weakly in the short term.

text:
DCE iron ore futures continued to decline sharply. The most-traded contract I2501 hit a new low of 706.5 yuan/mt, slightly rebounded in the afternoon,and finally closed at 713 yuan/mt, down 3.32% for the day. Some traders suspended offers; steel mills were cautious and mainly inquired about prices. Overall market transaction sentiment was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 735-740 yuan/mt, down 20- 25 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 745-750 yuan/mt, down 20-25 yuan/mt from yesterday. On August 14, the blast furnace operating rate surveyed by SMM was 91.42%, down 0.95% MoM. The daily pig iron production of sample steel mills was 2.2421 million mt, down 25,100 mt MoM. Pig iron production continued to decline significantly. Meanwhile, market rumors about possible crude steel production cuts in Tangshan heightened market concerns, leading to a sharp drop in iron ore prices. Given the potential rebound in pig iron production next week and the approaching peak season, downstream demand may marginally improve, limiting the downside space for iron ore prices, which are expected to remain weak and volatile.

DCE iron ore continued futures its weak oscillation. The most-traded contract I2501 fell below 700 points to 691 during the session and finallyclosed at 703.5, down 2.09% for the day. Market sentiment turned more cautious; traders showed low willingness to sell. Steel mills were cautiously observing and restocking as needed. Overall market transactions were average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 705- 720 yuan/mt, down 20-25 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 720-735 yuan/mt, down 20-25 yuan/mt from yesterday. Today, the total demand for the five major steel products slightly decreased MoM. With the reduction in total production, total inventory also correspondingly decreased. Additionally, various real estate indicators released by the statistics bureau today showed that the real estate industry is still declining. Market pessimism continued to spread, causing iron ore prices to hit new lows. Recently, the decline in material prices has exceeded that of finished products, leading to a recovery in steel mill profits and reducing the likelihood of further blast furnace maintenance, thereby providing some support for iron ore demand and prices.

Today, iron ore prices fluctuated, with the main contract I2501 experiencing a high and then a low, closing at 697, down 0.99% for the day.Some traders were unable to deliver on their contracts, indicating poor purchasing intentions from steel mills. The overall market atmosphere was quiet today, with limited trading activities. In Shandong, the price of PB powder ranged from 700-705 yuan/ton, a decrease of 5-10 yuan/ton from yesterday; while in Tangshan, the price ranged from 712-720 yuan/ton, a decrease of 5-10 yuan/ton from yesterday. As of August 16th, SMM tracked 35 port inventories totaling 147.16 million tons, an increase of 490,000 tons compared to the previous period and an increase of 29.83 million tons compared to the same period last year. The daily average import volume of ore is 3.086 million tons, an increase of 120,000 tons compared to the previous period, but a decrease of 88,000 tons compared to the same period last year. This week, iron ore prices hit a new low, prompting steel mills to replenish their stocks at low levels, leading to an increase in spot transaction volumes and port throughput. This indicates that there is still demand support for iron ore. Considering the lack of substantial improvement in end demand, it is expected that ore prices will continue to fluctuate at low levels.

Iron ore futures continued to trade in a strong and volatile manner today, with the main contract I2501 closing at 712, a 0.71% increase for the day.Traders followed the trend and shipped their goods accordingly. Steel mills remained cautious and only restocked necessary supplies. Overall, the market had a quiet atmosphere with low trading activity. In Shandong province, the price for PB powder ranged from 705-710 yuan per ton, an increase of 0-5 yuan per ton compared to the price last Friday. In Tangshan, the price for PB powder was at 720 yuan per ton, also a 0-5 yuan per ton increase from last week. According to SMM shipping data, global iron ore shipments totaled 30.54 million tons, a decrease of 4.2% compared to the previous period. Australian shipments saw a slight increase while Brazilian and non-mainstream mine shipments decreased. Chinese iron ore imports reached 25.35 million tons, a 2.89% decrease compared to the previous period. Despite global shipping volumes being low due to seasonality, domestic imports remained high, indicating a surplus in supply. End demand has not improved significantly and steel mills are facing severe losses, leading to a slight decrease in iron production but a narrower decrease compared to last week. Overall, the fundamentals of iron ore have slightly improved compared to last week, providing some support to ore prices.

Iron ore futures ﬂuctuated strongly, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 710.5 yuan/mt, up 1.21% for the day. Traders followed the markettrend to sell. Steel mills were cautiously observing, mainly making small and frequent purchases. The overall market transaction atmosphere was relatively average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 705- 710 yuan/mt, basically ﬂat compared to yesterday's prices; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 720-725 yuan/mt, up 0-5 yuan/ slightly, pig iron production remains on a downward trend, and end-user demand has not improved, resulting in insuffi- cient momentum for iron ore prices to rise. Under the pressure of negative feedback, iron ore prices ﬂuctuated at low levels.

snippet: 132.21 139.47 116.00 155.00 IRON ORE SEABORNE INDEX (IOS!) MARKET COMMENTARY Aug 20th, 2024 CFR Qingdao, USD/dry tonne Iron ore futures fluctuated strongly, with the most-traded contract [2501 closing

text:
Iron ore futures opened high and moved higher, with the most-traded contract I2501 surging significantly to close at 742, up 4.58% for the day.Traders' enthusiasm for selling increased noticeably. Steel mills were more cautious, with average purchasing intentions. The overall market transaction atmosphere was acceptable today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 725-730 yuan/mt, up 15-20 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 745-750 yuan/mt, up 15-20 yuan/mt from yesterday. Finished steel prices stabilized and rebounded, steel mill profits recovered somewhat, and expectations for improved demand in the peak season strengthened, boosting ferrous metals significantly. However, this week, SMM reported a blast furnace operating rate of 91.42%, down 0.95% WoW. Sample steel mills' daily pig iron production was 2.2421 million mt, down 25,100 mt WoW. Iron ore demand continues to decline, and pressure on iron ore remains, with limited upward momentum. Attention should be paid to the future improvement in apparent steel demand.

text:
Today, the iron ore futures opened high and then fell back, with the main contract I2501 closing at 730, up 0.41% for the day. The enthusiasmof traders to sell is moderate, while steel mills are more cautious and have average purchasing intentions. The overall market trading atmosphere today is relatively quiet. In Shandong, the price of PB powder transactions is in the range of 725-730 yuan/ton. In Tangshan, the price of PB powder transactions is around 745-750 yuan/ton, which is basically unchanged from yesterday. According to SMM's data on ten ports, there has been a noticeable decrease in port inventory compared to the previous period. From the perspective of the five major materials' apparent demand released today, there has been some improvement compared to before. The demand for hot-rolled products has improved significantly, which may drive enthusiasm in the raw materials market. In summary, it is expected that the short-term iron ore prices may fluctuate slightly stronger.

text:
Today, iron ore prices ran weak, accelerating their decline by the end of the session. The most-traded contract I2501 surged significantly, finallyclosing at 719.5 yuan/mt, with a daily drop of 2.24%. Traders' enthusiasm for selling weakened. Steel mills restocked as needed. Overall market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 720 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 735-740 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. As of August 23, total inventory at the 35 ports tracked by SMM was 147.13 million mt, down 30,000 mt MoM, up 30.02 million mt YoY. Daily average shipments from ports of imported ore were 2.899 million mt, down 187,000 mt MoM. This week, port congestion increased. On the supply side, steel mills' profits remained under pressure, coupled with the recent rebound in iron ore prices, leading steel mills to mainly restock as needed. Overall, iron ore demand remained weak, and iron ore prices fluctuated at low levels under pressure.

The iron ore futures market has seen a significant increase, with the main contract I2501 rising sharply to close at 750.5, up 3.45% for the day.Trading firms are actively shipping goods, while steel mills continue to focus on demand-based procurement, leading to a generally moderate trading atmosphere in the market. In Shandong, the transaction price for pellet feed powder is in the range of 745-750 yuan/ton, up by 20-25 yuan/ton compared to last Friday; in Tangshan, the transaction price is in the range of 760-765 yuan/ton, up by 20-25 yuan/ton from yesterday. SMM data shows that global iron ore shipments totaled 33.88 million tons, up by 10.9% on a monthly basis. Among them, shipments from Australia reached 17.9 million tons, up by 5.1% month-on-month; shipments from Brazil reached 7.35 million tons, up by 4.3% month-on- month, indicating a relatively loose overall supply. On the demand side, steel mills' profits are still under pressure, and there are still a considerable number of blast furnace maintenance shutdowns, which may suppress iron ore prices. It is expected that iron ore prices may ﬂuctuate in the short term.

Today, iron ore futures fluctuated strongly, with the most-traded contract I2501 surging significantly to close at 758, up 3.34% for the day.Traders were relatively active in selling. Steel mills had fewer inquiries, with some planning tenders. Overall market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 745-751 yuan/mt, up 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 765-775 yuan/mt, up 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. Recently, there has been a lot of macro news. On one hand, the issuance speed of special bonds has increased. On the other hand, as September approaches, the expectation of a rate cut by the US Fed has strengthened. Market sentiment has improved. Coupled with steel exports remaining at high levels, prices of various ferrous metals have rebounded. Considering that steel demand is still expected to improve marginally, iron ore prices are expected to fluctuate strongly.

text:
Today, iron ore futures were strong initially but weakened later. The most-traded contract I2501 finally closed at 754.5 yuan/mt, almost flatcompared to yesterday. Traders sold according to market conditions, and steel mills restocked as needed. The overall market transaction atmosphere was sluggish today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 745-750 yuan/mt, stable compared to yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 765 yuan/mt, also stable compared to yesterday. On August 28, the operaƟng rate of blast furnaces at 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 88.23%, down 0.56% MoM. The capacity utilisation rate of blast furnaces was 89.55%, down 1.03% MoM. The daily average pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.406 million mt, down 15,000 mt MoM. Based on the current blast furnace maintenance and production resumption plans, pig iron production may bottom out and rebound next week. With the expectation of production resumption, short-term ore prices may remain strong. Future attention should be paid to the end-user demand situation.

text:
Today, iron ore futures ﬂuctuated strongly, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 760 yuan/mt, up 0.53% for the day. Traders showed a fairwillingness to sell. Steel mills remained cautious, primarily restocking as needed. The overall market transaction atmosphere was decent today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 745-755 yuan/mt, up 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 760- 765 yuan/mt, unchanged from yesterday. Today, the apparent demand for the five major steel products showed an overall upward trend, with total inventory significantly reduced. The supply-demand mismatch for finished steel products was minimal. With the peak season approaching, the market holds high expectations for improved end-user demand, driving up the prices of the entire ferrous metals series. Additionally, the seventh round of coke price cuts has been implemented, further boosting steel mill profits. Due to profit recovery, more blast furnace production resumption plans are emerging, and pig iron production is expected to increase next week, providing some support for iron ore prices. In the short term, iron ore prices may continue to ﬂuctuate strongly.

Today, iron ore futures initially rose and then fell back from highs, experiencing wide ﬂuctuations throughout the day. The most-traded contract I2501finally closed at 754 yuan/mt, down 0.53% for the day. Traders sold goods according to market trends. Steel mills were cautious and their purchase willingness weakened. The overall market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 745-748 yuan/mt, falling back 0-7 yuan/mt from yesterday's highs; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 760 yuan/mt, falling back 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday's highs. As of August 30, the total inventory of 35 ports tracked by SMM was 150.47 million mt, up 3.34 million mt MoM and up 32.27 million mt YoY. The daily average port pick-up volume of imported ore was 2.87 million mt, down 30,000 mt MoM and down 150,000 mt YoY. Recently, ore prices have started to rebound, putting pressure on steel mill profits, leading them to restock as needed, which caused a slight decline in port pick-up volume. Port inventories have surged again, suppressing the rise in ore prices. However, considering the expected improvement in future end-user demand, iron ore demand may increase, and ore prices are expected to strengthen again next week.

text:
Today, iron ore futures saw a significant decline, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 723.5 yuan/mt, down 4.36% for the day. Traders showedlow willingness to sell. Steel mills increased their inquiries, mainly focusing on low-price, high-frequency purchases. The overall market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at 717-720 yuan/mt, down 20-25 yuan/mt WoW; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 735 yuan/mt, down 20-30 yuan/mt WoW. According to SMM shipping data, global iron ore total shipments last week were 29.73 million mt, down 12.2% WoW. Among them, shipments from Australia and non-mainstream mines saw a significant decline, while shipments from Brazil increased by 14.6% MoM. The total arrivals slightly decreased by 4.74% MoM. Overall, global iron ore supply decreased. Attention should be paid to the recovery of pig iron this week, and it is expected that the fundamentals of iron ore will improve. Additionally, considering monetary policy expectations, ore prices may see an increase.

text:
Today, iron ore futures continued to plummet, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 703.5 yuan/mt, down 4.37% for the day. Sometraders suspended offers and refrained from selling. Steel mills were cautious and chose to restock as needed. Today's market transactions were average. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 700 yuan/mt, down 15-20 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 715-720 yuan/mt, down 15-20 yuan/mt from yesterday. Over the weekend, the August PMI data was released at 49.1, far below market expectations. This weakened market confidence in the demand strength during the peak season. Additionally, the lack of favorable macroeconomic policies further dampened market sentiment. Under these circumstances, the resumption of blast furnace operations at steel mills faces greater pressure, and the expected increase in pig iron output is weak, puƫng pressure on iron ore prices. However, considering the current low valuation of iron ore, the existing prices have already suppressed shipments from non-mainstream mines, thus limiting the downside potential for iron ore prices. It is expected that iron ore prices will fluctuate at low levels in the short term.

text:
Today, iron ore futures continued to decline, with the most-traded contract I2501 falling below 700 points, ultimately closing at 689.5, down 3.09% for the day.Traders showed a low willingness to sell. Steel mills were cautiously observing the market, mainly engaging in small and frequent purchases. Today's market transactions were sluggish. In Shandong, the transaction price of PB fines was around 690-695 yuan/mt, down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction price of PB fines was around 705-710 yuan/mt, also down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. Last night, the ISM manufacturing PMI data released by the US fell short of market expectations, further raising concerns about the US manufacturing sector. Coupled with China's August PMI data released over the weekend, this led to a significant drop in ferrous metals series futures prices. From the perspective of iron ore fundamentals, the number of blast furnaces resuming production increased this week, with a slight rise in blast furnace operating rates and pig iron production. Although the pace of steel mills resuming production was slow, pig iron production is expected to increase significantly next week, which may provide some support for iron ore prices.

Today, Dalian iron ore futures continued to decline sharply, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 678.5 yuan/mt, down 2.58% for the day.Some traders halted offers. Steel mills restocked as needed. Market trading sentiment was relatively average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 680-685 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 700 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. The apparent demand for the five major steel products announced today was almost flat, with demand recovery falling short of expectaƟons, while supply increased. This deepened market concerns about future demand decline, further worsening market sentiment. In the short term, market sentiment appears overly pessimistic, and fundamentals have not shown significant improvement. It is expected that iron ore prices will fluctuate at low levels.

Today, iron ore futures fluctuated upward, with the most-traded contract 2501 closing at 685 yuan, up 0.44% throughout the day. Traders shipped based onmarket conditions. Steel mills were cautious and mainly restocked as needed. Today's market trading atmosphere was average. In Shandong, the PB fines transaction prices were around 688-690 yuan/mt, up 0-3 yuan/mt from last Friday; in Tangshan, PB fines transaction prices remained stable at 700-705 yuan/mt compared to last Friday. Last week, the SMM global total shipments of iron ore were 34.33 million mt, up 15.5% WoW. Shipments from Australia increased significantly by 20.9% WoW; shipments from Australia to China accounted for 87.3% of Australia's total shipments, a substantial increase of 33.9% WoW. Shipments from Brazil decreased by 2.4% WoW; shipments from Brazil to China accounted for 38.2% of Brazil's total shipments, up 18.5% WoW. Non-mainstream shipments significantly increased, but due to ore prices, the proportion of non-mainstream shipments to China decreased substantially. Additionally, an SMM survey indicated that cooler weather recently increased demand at some construction sites, boosting market confidence. Future observation of apparent demand data is needed. Considering that steel mill profits haven't significantly improved recently, the resumption of blast furnace production may be lower-than-expected, and iron ore prices are under pressure to fluctuate.

text:
Today, iron ore ﬂuctuated upward and plunged at the close. The most-traded contract I2501 finally settled at 675 yuan/mt, dropping 0.07%throughout the day. Traders were fairly active in oﬄoading their stocks. After the steel mills lowered prices, their cautious sentiment grew stronger, leading to a reduction in purchase willingness. Today's market trading atmosphere was average. The transaction price of PB fines in Shandong was around 678-690 yuan/mt, down 0-2 yuan/mt compared to yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction price of PB fines was around 692-705 yuan/mt, down 0-8 yuan/mt compared to yesterday. According to SMM statistics, the impact of blast furnace maintenance on pig iron production this week was 1.4196 million mt, down 35,800 mt WoW. Due to the slow growth in downstream demand, the resumption of blast furnace operations at steel mills has been delayed, making a significant increase in pig iron production unlikely in the short term. The upward momentum for ore prices is lacking, and they may continue to ﬂuctuate at low levels in the near term.

Today, iron ore opened low and moved higher, ﬂuctuating upward throughout the day. The most-traded contract I2501 closed at 694, up1.09% over the day. Traders showed a good willingness to sell, while speculative demand increased; some steel mills had restocking needs, enhancing their purchase willingness. Market transaction sentiment improved today. In the Shandong region, PB fines traded at around 690-695 yuan/mt, up by 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in the Tangshan region, PB fines traded at around 700-710 yuan/mt, up by 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to an SMM survey, on September 11, the operating rate of blast furnaces among 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 88.62%, up 0.26% WoW. The capacity utilisation rate of blast furnaces was 89.60%, up 0.03% WoW. The daily average pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.4072 million mt, up 800 mt WoW. In the short term, the increase in pig iron production is limited, but it is expected to gradually expand by mid-to-late September. However, the news of production restrictions in Tangshan may aﬀect market sentiment. Additionally, considering that some steel mills need to restock before the Mid- Autumn Festival, the iron ore market's long and short positions are intensifying, and the market may experience repeated ﬂuctuations in the short term.

Iron ore futures surged today. The most-traded contract I2501 finally closed at 707 yuan/mt, with a daily increase of 3.97%. Traders actively sold theirstocks; steel mills remained cautious and restocked as needed. The market trading atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines were traded at around 690-710 yuan/mt, up 10-20 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines were traded at around 700-720 yuan/mt, up 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. Today's rebar apparent demand data showed a significant increase, with a notable decline in the inventories of the five major steel products and a substantial rise in end-user demand. The overall market sentiment improved, driving ore prices sharply higher. Given that recent changes in steel mill profits have been negligible and the blast furnace resumption has been slow, there is insufficient drive for further increases in ore prices and limited room for them to rise further.

text:
Today, iron ore futures dropped significantly, ﬂuctuating downward throughout the day. The most-traded contract I2501 finally closed at675 yuan/ mt, down 4.12% for the day. Market sentiment turned more cautious, and traders showed a lower willingness to sell; steel mills mainly made low- price purchases, with some starting to restock before the holiday. Today's market trading atmosphere was sluggish. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 675-680 yuan/mt, down 15-20 yuan/mt from before the holiday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at around 695-700 yuan/mt, down 10-20 yuan/mt from before the holiday. During the holiday, the August social financing and real estate data were lower-than-expected, further dampening market sentiment, and iron ore prices returned to low levels. On the supply side, due to prices and domestic typhoon weather, the pressure on iron ore supply temporarily eased. Demand side, with the gradual resumption of blast furnaces in steel mills, pig iron production slightly increased. Additionally, with the National Day holiday approaching, some steel mills started to stock up in advance, improving the fundamentals of iron ore and providing some support to ore prices. Close attention should be paid to the US Fed's interest rate decision tomorrow.

Today, iron ore rebounded from its bottom and ﬂuctuated upward throughout the day. The most-traded contract I2501 finally closedat 693 yuan/ mt, with a daily increase of 1.69%. Speculative trading among traders increased; steel mills mainly remained on the sidelines, with some planning tenders. Today's market transaction atmosphere was average. The transaction price of PB fines in Shandong was around 675-695 yuan/mt, up 0-20 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction price of PB fines was around 695-715 yuan/mt, up 0-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. In the early morning, the FOMC meeting announced that the US Fed would cut interest rates by 50 basis points, slightly exceeding market expectations. During the period from the announcement to Powell's speech, the overseas market generally reacted with a "buy the rumor, sell the news" sentiment, causing iron ore futures to slightly retreat after opening. However, in the short term, the rate cut is beneficial to the real estate and manufacturing sectors. This also led to increased market expectations for macroeconomic policies in the fourth quarter, driving the futures market to rise rapidly. Driven by macro factors and pre-holiday restocking, it is expected that iron ore prices will continue to ﬂuctuate upward in the short term.

Today, Iron ore futures moved downwards after a higher opening, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 680 yuan/ mt, up 0.15% for the day.Traders showed a moderate willingness to sell, while steel mills restocked as needed. The market trading atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 685-695 yuan/mt, down 0-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 700-715 yuan/mt, remaining mostly stable compared to yesterday. The September Loan Prime Rate (LPR) remained unchanged, falling short of market expectations, leading to a slight correcƟon in the futures market. Looking ahead to next week, iron ore arrivals may continue to decrease due to the impact of the typhoon; however, supported by increased pig iron production and pre-holiday restocking demand, iron ore prices are expected to fluctuate upward.

text:
The iron ore market continued its downward trend, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 658.5, down 4.5% for the day.Traders showed a low willingness to sell; steel mills had more inquiries, mainly restocking as needed. The market atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 665-670 yuan/mt, down 25-30 yuan/mt WoW from last Friday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 685-690 yuan/mt, down 15-30 yuan/mt WoW from last Friday. SMM reported global iron ore total shipments at 35.53 million mt, up 14.4% WoW. Shipments from Australia and Brazil increased, as did those from non-mainstream mines. However, due to low ore prices, the shipment increase from non-mainstream mines was relatively small. The significant supply increase negatively impacted ore prices, combined with inventory at high levels at ports, puƫng further pressure on prices. Considering pig iron is in a recovery phase and pre-holiday restocking is boosting overall iron ore demand, there is some support for ore prices, and the short-term downside is expected to be limited.

Today, iron ore futures opened low and closed high, with a significant increase throughout the day. The most-traded contract I2501closed at 699.5 yuan/mt, up 4.64% for the day. Traders were moderately active in selling, and speculative transactions slightly increased; steel mills were more cautious, with some restocking as needed. The market transaction atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 685-705 yuan/mt, up 20-35 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 710-720 yuan/mt, also up 20-35 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to SMM statistics, blast furnace maintenance reduced production by 93,300 mt this week, a significant decrease WoW. The reduction is expected to continue expanding next week, boosting iron ore demand. Additionally, most steel mills needed to restock before the holiday, providing strong support for ore prices. Meanwhile, the central bank announced a series of growth-stabilizing real estate policies today, including lowering down payments and existing mortgage rates, which boosted market macro sentiment and led to a significant rise in futures. In the short term, ore prices may continue to ﬂuctuate upward.

text:
Today, iron ore futures continued to fluctuate upward, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 709, up 4.19% for the day.Traders showed a good willingness to sell, while steel mills remained cautious, with some restocking as needed. Today's market trading atmosphere was weaker than yesterday. In Shandong, PB fines traded at around 705-710 yuan/mt, up 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, PB fines traded at 720-725 yuan/mt, also up 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to an SMM survey, on September 25, the operating rate of blast furnaces in 242 surveyed steel mills was 89.40%, up 0.65% WoW. The daily pig iron production of sample steel mills was 2.4252 million mt, up 13,600 mt WoW. Meanwhile, favorable market policies continued to be announced, boosting market sentiment, and iron ore futures prices continued to rise. However, high port inventory levels suppressed spot price increases, narrowing the spread between futures and spot prices. In the short term, iron ore futures prices may continue to fluctuate upward, but the momentum for spot price increases appears insufficient.

This briefing aimed to provide insights on the agenda for climate emissions and marine pollution discussions at the forthcoming82nd session of the International Maritime Organization's (IMO) Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC 82, 30 September - 4 October 2024). The event presented the Clean Arctic Alliance's expectations and recommendations for this meeting, and what is at stake for black carbon, ECAs, scrubbers, underwater noise, GHGs, plastics and biodiversity.
Source: Clean Arctic Alliance

text:
Today, iron ore futures fluctuated, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 783 yuan, up 0.32% for the day. Traders were actively selling,while steel mills remained cautious and restocked as needed. The market trading atmosphere was average. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 770-775 yuan/mt, basically stable compared to yesterday's spot prices; in Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 780-785 yuan/mt, up 1-5 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to SMM statistics, this week (November 23 to November 29), the impact on pig iron production due to blast furnace maintenance was 1.4846 million mt, up 65,400 mt WoW. Recently, pig iron production from steel mill blast furnaces has shown a downward trend, indicating a weakening market in the short term. It is expected that iron ore prices will remain weak and fluctuate in the near term.

Today, iron ore ﬂuctuated upward, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 792 yuan, up 1.08% for the day. Traders were activelyselling, while steel mills remained cautious and had moderate purchase willingness. The market trading atmosphere was moderate. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 775-780 yuan/mt, up 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction prices for PB fines were 790-795 yuan/mt, also up 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to an SMM survey, on November 27, the operating rate of blast furnaces in 242 surveyed steel mills was 89.16%, down 0.67% WoW. The capacity utilisation rate of blast furnaces was 89.75%, down 0.80% WoW. The daily pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.4 million mt, down 21,500 mt WoW. The fundamentals of iron ore continued to weaken. However, market rumors suggested that the Politburo meeting in December might be held earlier, which boosted market expectations. Additionally, some steel mills started purchasing imported cargo to increase inventory, providing strong support for ore prices.

Today, iron ore futures moved downwards after a higher opening, with the most-traded contract I2501 finally closing at 786.5 yuan/mt,maintaining stability throughout the day. Traders sold goods according to market trends, while steel mills restocked as needed. The market trading atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 775-780 yuan/mt, unchanged from yesterday; in Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 785-790 yuan/mt, down by 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday. Today, the apparent demand for rebar slightly decreased, while inventory increased slightly. The demand for construction materials has entered the oﬀ-season, and with the impact of future weather conditions, demand is expected to weaken further. Additionally, rumors of production control at a certain steel mill have led to market expectations of weaker iron ore demand, suppressing ore prices at low levels. Given that some steel mills have already started stockpiling for the Chinese New Year, the forward spot market remains active, providing some support for iron ore prices. Iron ore prices are expected to strengthen again after a short-term consolidation.

text:
Today, Dalian iron ore futures ﬂuctuated upward, with the most-traded I2501 contract closing at 797.5 yuan/mt, up 1.14% for the day. Tradersactively sold oﬀ their stocks, while steel mills remained cautious, with some mills locking in profits through good sales of finished products and increasing their procurement volume of raw materials. The market trading atmosphere was moderate today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 780-785 yuan/mt, up 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 795-800 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. As of November 29, the total inventory at the 35 ports monitored by SMM was 147.3 million mt, down 1.56 million mt WoW but up 35.23 million mt YoY. The daily average port pick-up volume for imported ore was 3.26 million mt, up 80,000 mt MoM and up 310,000 mt YoY. This week, factory shipments were good, and some steel mills began restocking as winter approached, driving the increase in port pick-up volume. Looking ahead to next week, macro expectations are trengthening, and ore prices are expected to continue ﬂuctuating upward.

Today, iron ore ﬂuctuated upward, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 806 yuan/mt, up 1.26% for the day. Traders are optimistic about the market outlookand are actively selling; however, steel mills are cautiously observing, resulting in a decrease in inquiries. The market trading atmosphere was moderate today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 790-795 yuan/mt, up 10 yuan/mt compared to last Friday; in Tangshan, the transaction price for PB fines was 805 yuan/mt, also up 10 yuan/mt compared to last Friday. Last week, SMM reported global iron ore total shipments of 33.35 million mt, up 1.4% WoW. Both Australia and Brazil saw increases in total shipments, but the proportion shipped to China slightly decreased. Additionally, due to previous shipment declines and domestic weather impacts, SMM reported China's total iron ore arrivals at 25 million mt, down 5.27% WoW. In the short term, the market may continue to operate at low levels. However, as the meeting approaches, market expectations for the meeting are growing stronger, driving iron ore prices to continue rising. In the short term, the market may continue to ﬂuctuate upward.

Today, iron ore ﬂuctuated upward, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 806 yuan/mt, up 1.26% for the day. Traders are optimistic about the market outlookand are actively selling; however, steel mills are cautiously observing, resulting in a decrease in inquiries. The market trading atmosphere was moderate today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 790-795 yuan/mt, up 10 yuan/mt compared to last Friday; in Tangshan, the transaction price for PB fines was 805 yuan/mt, also up 10 yuan/mt compared to last Friday. Last week, SMM reported global iron ore total shipments of 33.35 million mt, up 1.4% WoW. Both Australia and Brazil saw increases in total shipments, but the proportion shipped to China slightly decreased. Additionally, due to previous shipment declines and domestic weather impacts, SMM reported China's total iron ore arrivals at 25 million mt, down 5.27% WoW. In the short term, the market may continue to operate at low levels. However, as the meeting approaches, market expectations for the meeting are growing stronger, driving iron ore prices to continue rising. In the short term, the market may continue to ﬂuctuate upward.

text:
Today, iron ore futures continued to ﬂuctuate, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 812 yuan, up 0.43% for the day. Traders showed moderateenthusiasm for selling, with a strong wait-and-see sentiment; steel mills were cautious in their inquiries, primarily purchasing as needed. The market trading atmosphere was generally average today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 798 yuan/mt, up 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction prices for PB fines were 810 yuan/mt, basically ﬂat from yesterday. According to an SMM survey, on December 4, the operating rate of blast furnaces at 242 surveyed steel mills was 88.94%, down 0.22% MoM. The daily average pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.4101 million mt, up 10,100 mt MoM. In the short term, steel mill profits slightly improved, providing some support for ore prices. Coupled with the market's positive expectations for upcoming major meetings, iron ore prices are expected to have room for further upward movement in the short term.

text:
Today, iron ore futures opened higher but moved downwards, continuing to fluctuate downward throughout the day. The most-tradedcontract I2501 finally closed at 800.5 yuan/mt, down 1.17% for the day. Traders' enthusiasm for selling has somewhat declined; steel mills' purchase willingness is moderate, mainly purchasing as needed. Today's market trading atmosphere was average. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 785 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction prices for PB fines were 800-810 yuan/mt, down 0-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. Today's industry data performed moderately, with a slight increase in apparent demand for rebar and a slight decrease in inventory. However, end-use demand has entered the off-season, and there is still an expectation of marginal weakening in the future. Additionally, with the meeting approaching, market rumors are increasing, and the annual GDP growth forecast is being revised downward, leading to more pessimistic market sentiment. Considering that pre-holiday restocking of iron ore has gradually begun, providing some support for prices, iron ore prices are expected to rise after adjustments.

Today, iron ore ﬂuctuated downward throughout the day, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 797.5 yuan/mt, down 0.93% for the day.Traders showed moderate willingness to sell; steel mills remained cautious, with some planning tenders. Today's market sentiment was sluggish. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 780-785 yuan/mt, down 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 795-800 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. Looking ahead to next week, the fundamentals of iron ore are expected to remain stable. The main price drivers will be the impact of two important meetings on market sentiment. Next week, market expectations are likely to remain positive, and iron ore prices may ﬂuctuate upward.

text:
Today, iron ore futures ﬂuctuated upward throughout the day, with the most-traded contract I2501 closing at 808.5 yuan/mt, up 1.57% for the day.Traders were actively selling, while steel mills remained cautious and purchased as needed. The market trading atmosphere was average today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 790-795 yuan/mt, up 10 yuan/mt compared to last Friday; in Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 805-810 yuan/mt, up 10 yuan/mt compared to last Friday. Today's Central Political Bureau meeting conveyed numerous positive signals, boosting market sentiment and enhancing confidence in China's economy for 2025. This drove up ore prices. From a fundamental perspective, last week's SMM data showed a significant decline in global shipments. On the demand side, due to environmental protection-driven production restrictions in Handan, Hebei, some steel mills plan to shut down blast furnaces for maintenance, which is expected to significantly reduce pig iron production. In the short term, although the supply and demand fundamentals of the iron ore market remain weak, prices may continue to ﬂuctuate upward under the inﬂuence of optimistic macro sentiment.

text:
Today, Dalian iron ore futures opened higher and continued to rise, reaching a peak of 833 yuan/mt before slightly retreating.The most-traded contract I2501 fluctuated upward throughout the day and finally closed at 817 yuan/mt, up 1.87% for the day. Traders were actively selling, while steel mills remained cautious with moderate purchase willingness. Market transactions were relatively few today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 795-800 yuan/mt, up 5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction prices for PB fines were 810-815 yuan/mt, up 5- 10 yuan/mt from yesterday. Yesterday's Politburo meeting released several positive signals, indicating that future monetary and fiscal policies will be relatively loose, which significantly boosted market sentiment. However, according to SMM's survey on blast furnace maintenance, due to environmental protection-driven production restrictions in Hebei, many steel mills were forced to shut down and maintain their blast furnaces. The impact from maintenance increased by more than 200,000 mt WoW. This weakened the demand for iron ore, limiting the rise in ore prices. Nevertheless, considering the upcoming economic conference, market sentiment remains optimistic, and ore prices are expected to maintain a fluctuating upward trend in the short term.

Today, the iron ore market underwent a contract rollover, with the most-traded contract switching to the I2505 contract.It remained stable in the morning but slightly declined in the afternoon. Throughout the day, it fluctuated downward, ultimately closing at 802, with a daily drop of 0.8%. Traders showed moderate willingness to sell, while steel mills purchased as needed. Today's market transaction atmosphere was average. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 790-795 yuan/mt, down 5 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction prices for PB fines were 800-805 yuan/mt, also down 5 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to an SMM survey, on December 11, the operating rate of blast furnaces in 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 86.23%, down 2.71 percentage points MoM. The daily pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.3626 million mt, down 47,500 mt MoM. Recently, due to environmental protection-driven production restrictions in Hebei, many blast furnaces in steel mills have been shut down, leading to a significant decline in pig iron production. This has caused iron ore prices to fluctuate downward. Considering that important meetings are still being held recently, the downward space for iron ore is relatively limited. Attention should be paid to the impact of economic meeƟng content on market sentiment.

text:
Iron ore futures opened lower and closed higher today. The market ﬂuctuated upward throughout the day, finally closingat 812.5, up 1.25% for the day. Traders showed good enthusiasm for selling, while steel mills purchased as needed. Market transactions were quiet today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 795-800 yuan/mt, up 5 yuan/mt from yesterday. In Tangshan, the transaction prices for PB fines were 805-810 yuan/mt, up 5 yuan/mt from yesterday. According to today's SMM industry data, the apparent demand for five major steel products slightly increased again. Total inventory continued to decline. The supply-demand imbalance for finished steel products remained moderate and continued to accumulate. In terms of market news, there were rumors that the important economic work conference had concluded, with some positive policy signals circulating. These reports boosted market sentiment to some extent, driving the strong rise in iron ore prices.

text:
Today, iron ore fluctuated downward and finally closed at 797, with a daily decline of 1.12%. Traders shipped goods in linewith the market; steel mills reduced inquiries, and some have tender plans. The market transactions were sluggish today. In the Shandong region, the mainstream transaction prices for PB powder were around 790 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in the Tangshan region, the transaction prices for PB powder were around 805 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. The central economic meeting held yesterday essentially continued the spirit of the previous political meetings and was in line with market expectations. As short-term macro policies are gradually implemented, the market focus has returned to fundamentals. Affected by environmental protectiondriven production restrictions in Hebei, pig iron production may slightly decrease, leading to weakened demand for iron ore and a sluggish fluctuation in ore prices. However, considering the potential for RRR cuts next week and the relatively small supply-demand imbalance in the industry chain, iron ore prices are expected to fluctuate at high levels next week.

text:
Today, iron ore fluctuated downward and finally closed at 797, with a daily decline of 1.12%. Traders shipped goods in linewith the market; steel mills reduced inquiries, and some have tender plans. The market transactions were sluggish today. In the Shandong region, the mainstream transaction prices for PB powder were around 790 yuan/mt, down 10 yuan/mt from yesterday; in the Tangshan region, the transaction prices for PB powder were around 805 yuan/mt, down 5-10 yuan/mt from yesterday. The central economic meeting held yesterday essentially continued the spirit of the previous political meetings and was in line with market expectations. As short-term macro policies are gradually implemented, the market focus has returned to fundamentals. Affected by environmental protectiondriven production restrictions in Hebei, pig iron production may slightly decrease, leading to weakened demand for iron ore and a sluggish fluctuation in ore prices. However, considering the potential for RRR cuts next week and the relatively small supply-demand imbalance in the industry chain, iron ore prices are expected to fluctuate at high levels next week.

text:
Today, DCE iron ore futures rose initially but then fell, with the most-traded I2505 contract closing at 796.5 yuan/mt, up0.06% for the day. Traders showed moderate enthusiasm for selling, while steel mills purchased as needed. Market transactions were moderate today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices of PB fines were around 790 yuan/mt, stable compared to yesterday. In Tangshan, PB fines were traded at 800-805 yuan/mt, also stable compared to yesterday. In Handan, Hebei, most blast furnaces at steel mills affected by environmental protection-driven production restrictions have resumed operaƟons. However, as year-end approaches, annual maintenance plans have increased. According to SMM survey data on blast furnace maintenance, this week, the impact from maintenance on pig iron output was 1.8448 million mt, up 221,300 mt WoW. More blast furnace maintenance is planned for next week, with the estimated impact at 1.897 million mt, though the WoW increase is expected to narrow. The reduction in pig iron output has led to a decline in overall demand for iron ore, and iron ore prices are expected to remain stable with a weak trend in the short term.

Today, iron ore futures fluctuated downward. The most-traded I2505 contract finally closed at 778.5 yuan/mt, down 2.63%throughout the day. Traders showed a weak willingness to sell, while steel mills were cautiously observing, with a slight increase in purchase willingness. Market transactions were average today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices of PB fines were 775-780 yuan/mt, down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. In Tangshan, the transaction prices of PB fines were around 790 yuan/mt, also down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. This week, iron ore demand declined again. According to an SMM survey, as of December 18, the operating rate of blast furnaces at 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 85.47%, down 0.76 percentage points WoW. The capacity utilisation rate of blast furnaces was 87.01%, down 0.56 percentage points WoW. The daily pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.3476 million mt, down 15,000 mt WoW. The number of blast furnace maintenance cases continued to increase this week, mainly due to annual plans and environmental protection-driven production restrictions. In the short term, this situation is expected to persist, with a slight decline in pig iron production still possible in the near term.

text:
Today, iron ore futures fluctuated downward. The most-traded I2505 contract finally closed at 778.5 yuan/mt, down 2.63%throughout the day. Traders showed a weak willingness to sell, while steel mills were cautiously observing, with a slight increase in purchase willingness. Market transactions were average today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices of PB fines were 775-780 yuan/mt, down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. In Tangshan, the transaction prices of PB fines were around 790 yuan/mt, also down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday.This week, iron ore demand declined again. According to an SMM survey, as of December 18, the operating rate of blast furnaces at 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 85.47%, down 0.76 percentage points WoW. The capacity utilisation rate of blast furnaces was 87.01%, down 0.56 percentage points WoW. The daily pig iron production of the sample steel mills was 2.3476 million mt, down 15,000 mt WoW. The number of blast furnace maintenance cases continued to increase this week, mainly due to annual plans and environmental protection-driven production restrictions. In the short term, this situation is expected to persist, with a slight decline in pig iron production still possible in the near term.

Today, iron ore futures continued to drop slightly, with the most-traded I2505 contract closing at 769 yuan/mt, down 0.77% for the day.Traders showed low enthusiasm for selling, while steel mills remained cautious and exhibited average purchase willingness. Market transactions were sluggish today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were at 765-770 yuan/mt, down 5 yuan/mt from yesterday. In Tangshan, PB fines transaction prices were around 780 yuan/mt, also down 5 yuan/mt from yesterday. As of December 20, total inventory at 35 ports monitored by SMM stood at 145.85 million mt, down 810,000 mt WoW but up 30.23 million mt YoY. The daily average port pick-up volume of imported ore was 3.132 million mt, down 109,000 mt MoM but up 670,000 mt YoY. Affected by annual maintenance at some steel mills and environmental protection-driven production restrictions, pig iron production declined significantly. Coupled with falling ore prices, steel mills' purchase willingness weakened, leading to a notable drop in port pick-up volume. Looking ahead to next week, the fundamentals of iron ore are expected to remain weak, with ore prices likely to continue fluctuating downward.

Today, The iron ore futures opened lower but closed higher, fluctuating upward throughout the day. The most-traded I2505 contractfinally settled at 780 yuan/mt, up 0.84% for the day. Some traders with higher costs showed weak willingness to sell, while steel mills remained cautious with weak purchase willingness. Market transactions were sluggish today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were 775-778 yuan/mt, up 5 yuan/mt WoW from last Friday. In Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 785-790 yuan/mt, up 5-10 yuan/mt WoW from last Friday. SMM reported global iron ore shipments at 32.53 million mt, up 1.8% WoW. Among them, Australian shipments decreased slightly by 4.3% WoW, while Brazil's shipments surged significantly by 29.6% WoW. With previous influencing factors resolved, Brazil's shipments increased notably this week. Iron ore supply remains ample. Additionally, pig iron production is still expected to decline this week. Considering that steel mills have gradually started pre-holiday restocking, traders' sentiment to stand firm on quotes is relatively strong, which may provide some short-term support for ore prices.

text:
Today, DCE iron ore fluctuated during the day and rose slightly by the close. The most-traded I2505 contract finally settled at783 yuan/mt, up 1.29% throughout the day. Traders sold goods based on market trends, while steel mills remained cautious and purchased as needed. Market transactions were moderate today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices of PB fines were 775-780 yuan/mt, up 0-5 yuan/mt from yesterday. In Tangshan, the transaction prices of PB fines were 785-790 yuan/mt, basically flat compared to yesterday. According to the SMM survey, as of December 18, the operating rate of blast furnaces at 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 85.47%, down 0.76 percentage points MoM. The capacity utilisation rate of blast furnaces was 87.01%, down 0.56 percentage points MoM. The daily pig iron production of the sampled steel mills averaged 2.3476 million mt, down 15,000 mt MoM. Demand for iron ore continued to decline. However, this afternoon, the National Financial Work Conference concluded, and CCTV's interpretation of the meeting highlighted a more proactive fiscal policy, with fiscal funds for 2025 to be allocated earlier, faster, and in larger amounts. This stimulated market sentiment, driving iron ore prices to strengthen.

text:
Today, iron ore futures dropped significantly. The most-traded I2505 contract closed at 759.5 yuan/mt, down 2.63% from yesterday.Traders showed weak willingness to sell, while steel mills made limited purchases. Market transaction sentiment was sluggish today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were around 760 yuan/mt, down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday; in Tangshan, transaction prices for PB fines were 775 yuan/mt, also down 10-15 yuan/mt from yesterday. As of December 27, according to SMM monitoring data, total inventory at 35 ports stood at 144.99 million mt, down 860,000 mt WoW but up 28.15 million mt YoY. The daily port pick-up volume of imported ore averaged 3.127 million mt, down 4,000 mt MoM but up 270,000 mt YoY. Affected by earlier ore shipment volumes, this week's port arrivals dropped significantly. On the port cargo pick-up side, winter stockpiling by steel mills was not active, with most adopting a purchasing-as-needed strategy, leading to a slight decline in port pick-up volume. Overall, due to the significant drop in port arrivals, port inventory showed a destocking trend. Looking ahead to next week, port arrivals are expected to increase. Based on SMM's current tracking, pig iron production at steel mills' blast furnaces may continue to decline, and port pick-up volume may also decrease, potentially leading to a slight accumulation in port inventory.

text:
Today, DCE iron ore futures opened lower but moved higher, fluctuating upward throughout the day. The most-traded I2505 contract finallyclosed at 775.5 yuan/mt, up slightly by 0.98% for the day. Traders showed moderate willingness to sell, while steel mills remained cautious, with limited inquiries. The market transaction atmosphere was moderate today. In Shandong, mainstream transaction prices for PB fines were around 770-775 yuan/mt, up 10-15 yuan/mt from last Friday. In Tangshan, PB fines transaction prices were 785-790 yuan/mt, also up 10-15 yuan/mt from last Friday. Last week, SMM reported global iron ore shipments at 34.74 million mt, up 6.8% WoW. Among them, Australian shipments were 19.49 million mt, up 9.6% WoW, while Brazilian shipments were 8.04 million mt, down slightly by 1.2% WoW. SMM also reported China's iron ore arrivals at 25.75 million mt, up 1.9% WoW. Both shipments and arrivals increased simultaneously. Iron ore supply remained ample. However, the industry imbalance was relatively small, with steel mills still maintaining profits, and pig iron production may have hit bottom and stabilized. In the short term, iron ore prices are expected to fluctuate rangebound.

Today, Dalian iron ore fluctuated upward throughout the day. The most-traded I2505 contract finally closed at 779, rising slightlyby 1.17% for the day. Traders followed the market trend to sell goods, while steel mills remained cautious with fewer inquiries. The market transaction atmosphere was sluggish today. In Shandong, the mainstream transaction prices of PB fines were around 775 yuan/mt, remaining stable compared to yesterday; in Tangshan, the transaction prices of PB fines were 785-790 yuan/mt, also stable compared to yesterday. There was no macro news in the market today. From a fundamental perspective, the operating rate of blast furnaces at 242 steel mills surveyed by SMM was 85.37%, down 0.1 percentage points WoW. The daily pig iron production of sample steel mills was 2.3446 million mt, down 3,000 mt WoW. This week, overall demand for iron ore declined again. However, due to the expectation of pre-holiday restocking, ore prices continued to remain relatively stable.
